hyperedges.label: Helpers available to analyzers under the analyzer contract
Places that must change together when a verdict status is added

nodes.label: Generated app.js bundle (classic script IIFE)
nodes.rationale: Source is ES modules under src/ so it can be unit-tested in Node; the build concatenates them into one classic script so index.html works when opened from file:// as well as over HTTP. Consequences: unique top-level names across modules (build fails loudly), only relative ./x.js imports and named export declarations, app.js regenerated after every src/ change and never edited by hand.

nodes.label: Module dependency order sections->checks->config-parser->broker->analyzers->checklist->xlsx->report->ui->main
nodes.rationale: The bundle is a plain concatenation with one shared scope, so lower modules must never import higher ones; ORDER in scripts/build.mjs encodes the same sequence.

nodes.label: Data flow: file -> classifyFile -> detectHostname -> broker -> buildProfile -> buildChecklist/analyzeCheck -> UI table + buildWorkbook
nodes.norm_label: data flow: file -> classifyfile -> detecthostname -> broker -> buildprofile -> buildchecklist/analyzecheck -> ui table + buildworkbook

nodes.label: Analyzer contract: ANALYZERS[ref] = (ctx) => result(...) | null
nodes.rationale: ctx = { check, profile, profiles, targets, now }. Returning null falls back to defaultOutcome (Info dump of found sections, or Missing with a hint about gather-diagnostics vs supplemental). Analyzer exceptions are caught and surfaced as Info with an 'Analyzer error' note so one bad regex never blanks a whole column.

nodes.label: CLI section extraction (gather-diagnostics headers + prompt transcripts)
nodes.rationale: parseSections recognises two formats in the same file: '# CLI command:' header blocks and 'hostname> show ...' prompt lines. Sections are keyed by the normalised command; a check's commands may list '|' alternatives with first match wins. Supplemental transcripts are merged over diagnostics and profile.sectionSources records provenance so the UI can label the source.
nodes.norm_label: cli section extraction (gather-diagnostics headers + prompt transcripts)

nodes.label: Broker profile (role, version, snapshot, management IPs, config facts)
nodes.rationale: Role from 'show redundancy detail' (Configuration Status Disabled -> Standalone, Operating Mode Monitoring Node -> Monitor, Active-Standby Role Primary/Backup) falling back to the '*' row of 'show redundancy group'; columns sorted Primary, Backup, Monitor. A router-name mismatch between config and diagnostics becomes a profile warning shown on the card and in the Summary sheet.
nodes.norm_label: broker profile (role, version, snapshot, management ips, config facts)

nodes.label: Diagnostics snapshot time as reference date
nodes.rationale: Certificate expiry and days-remaining are computed against the diagnostics snapshot ('Last Refreshed' from show storage-element * detail, then SMRP/SEMP/RDP log timestamps), not today's date, because the bundle may be reviewed long after capture; ctx.now is only the fallback and the 1.8.2 output says which reference date applied.
nodes.norm_label: diagnostics snapshot time as reference date

nodes.label: Credential redaction at parse time (redactLine in parseConfig)
nodes.rationale: Password, secret and key values are masked while the current-config tree is built, before anything can reach the results table, the workbook or dev-script logs; never bypassed.
nodes.norm_label: credential redaction at parse time (redactline in parseconfig)

nodes.label: Indentation-tree config parser with explicit-path facts
nodes.rationale: parseConfig builds a tree from two-space indentation, ignores 'exit' lines and collects '!' comments separately ('! Router:' gives the router name). Every fact is read from an explicit path so the shutdown of a client-username is never confused with the shutdown of a message-vpn.
nodes.norm_label: indentation-tree config parser with explicit-path facts

nodes.label: Minimal XLSX/ZIP writer
nodes.rationale: xlsx.js knows nothing about the checklist: it writes inline strings, sanitises XML-invalid characters, truncates to Excel's 32,767-character cell limit, freezes two header rows and two columns, and puts the autofilter on row 2 (so no vertical merges there). Deliberately minimal (fixed styles, no formulas) so it needs no dependency and opens in Excel and LibreOffice.

nodes.label: Fail uses a soft red fill
nodes.rationale: Fill colours follow the Solace 2025 palette; the palette has no red, so Fail deliberately uses a soft red in both workbook fills and UI pills.
nodes.norm_label: fail uses a soft red fill

nodes.label: Adding a check walkthrough
nodes.rationale: Row in CHECKS (unique three-segment ref, '|' command alternatives) -> ANALYZERS[ref] -> add to GATHER_DIAGNOSTICS_COMMANDS only if the standard bundle produces it (otherwise it joins the supplemental list automatically) -> fixture section + assertion in analyzers.test.js -> scripts/dev.sh all.

nodes.label: Add a broker form (one broker at a time)
nodes.rationale: cli-diagnostics.txt required plus optional current-config export; hostname read from diagnostics and editable; a 'config' file that is really CLI output is attached as a supplemental transcript instead.
nodes.norm_label: add a broker form (one broker at a time)

nodes.label: Bulk import of gather-diagnostics folders
nodes.rationale: Kind and hostname detected per file so primary, backup and monitor bundles can be dropped together; system folders (usr/, var/, tmp/) and binary files are skipped; both paths converge on the same attach() call.

nodes.label: Assignment tray for files without a detected hostname
nodes.norm_label: assignment tray for files without a detected hostname

nodes.label: Verdict statuses: Pass / Warning / Fail / Info / Manual / N/A / Missing
nodes.rationale: Verdicts stay conservative: Warning = evidence needs a look or justification, Fail = evidence contradicts the expected result outright, Info = captured but design-dependent, Manual = no CLI evidence can answer, N/A = role/feature not applicable, Missing = sections not uploaded (note names the command). Adding a status requires updating STATUS_LABEL, STATUS_ORDER, UI pills and STATUS_STYLE in the same change.
nodes.norm_label: verdict statuses: pass / warning / fail / info / manual / n/a / missing

nodes.label: Supplemental CLI transcript
nodes.rationale: gather-diagnostics does not run show message-vpn * detail, client-profile, ACL, queue, LDAP/OAuth, syslog or backup commands; the tool exports the missing command list so operators run them with paging off and drop the transcript, each output preceded by its 'hostname> show ...' prompt line.

nodes.label: Current-config export (show current-config all)
nodes.rationale: Fallback evidence for the same checks when no transcript exists; also gives default objects, downgrade flags, queue subscriptions. Credentials are redacted before display.

nodes.label: Design targets (SolOS version, connection tier, spool MB)
nodes.rationale: Optional targets turn checks 1.1.5, 1.1.8 and 1.2.2 from Info into Pass/Fail because the expected values are design-specific and cannot be inferred from the broker alone.
nodes.norm_label: design targets (solos version, connection tier, spool mb)

nodes.label: Workbook: Summary, Readiness Checklist, Supplemental Commands sheets
nodes.norm_label: workbook: summary, readiness checklist, supplemental commands sheets

nodes.label: Role awareness: HA-pair checks return na on Monitor and Standalone
nodes.rationale: Redundancy checks are meaningless on a monitor or standalone node, so they must not appear as failures; 1.2.3 expects Enabled (Primary) or Enabled (Backup) according to the detected role.
nodes.norm_label: role awareness: ha-pair checks return na on monitor and standalone

nodes.label: Evidence is read from sections, not guessed
nodes.rationale: Prefer valueOf, counterOf, blockBetween, parseFixedTable over whole-body regexes so verdicts are anchored to specific CLI fields and survive unrelated output changes.
nodes.norm_label: evidence is read from sections, not guessed

nodes.label: DOM only in ui.js/main.js, scoped to createApp root
nodes.rationale: Every other module must load and run in Node so the node:test suites and lint can exercise the whole pipeline without a browser; ui.js never uses document.getElementById or globals for application state.
nodes.norm_label: dom only in ui.js/main.js, scoped to createapp root

nodes.label: Fixtures stay anonymised
nodes.rationale: No customer hostnames, IPs, organisation names, certificate serials or real passwords may enter the repo; real bundles are for manual checks only.

nodes.label: Gates: scripts/dev.sh all (build + lint + test), ask don't run
nodes.rationale: After any change under src/, test/, scripts/ or index.html the user runs ./scripts/dev.sh all and results are read from scripts/logs/<task>.log; generating app.js may be done by the author because the page cannot work without it, but lint and tests belong to the user. readiness_run.sh --check runs the gates and must not be invoked by the assistant.
nodes.norm_label: gates: scripts/dev.sh all (build + lint + test), ask don't run

nodes.label: Docs in sync: README + docs/*.md updated with behaviour changes
nodes.norm_label: docs in sync: readme + docs/*.md updated with behaviour changes

nodes.label: Mirrored dev scripts dev.sh / dev.ps1 (build, lint, test, all, serve)
nodes.rationale: Both shells behave identically and write scripts/logs/<task>.log fresh per run as plain UTF-8; read the log rather than console scrollback on failure. Tests are passed as a file glob because Node treats a bare directory as a file.
nodes.norm_label: mirrored dev scripts dev.sh / dev.ps1 (build, lint, test, all, serve)

nodes.label: node:test suites (sections, config-parser, broker, analyzers, xlsx)
nodes.norm_label: node:test suites (sections, config-parser, broker, analyzers, xlsx)

nodes.label: Pending /init-devops plan (tag-triggered CI, vet/cov/scan/full tasks, zipped static-site release)
nodes.rationale: No CI or remote yet; until approved the release artifact is the folder itself: index.html, styles.css, a freshly built app.js and README.md.
nodes.norm_label: pending /init-devops plan (tag-triggered ci, vet/cov/scan/full tasks, zipped static-site release)

nodes.label: Solace 2025 theme tokens (--sol-*, --sem-*)
nodes.rationale: Palette and typography live as CSS custom properties at the top of styles.css; status colours are semantic (--sem-*) and shared between UI pills and workbook fills so the two views agree.
